text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Glafcos Clerides and Rauf Denktash are edging closer to talks. Athens supports their resumption provided the Turkish side is ready to abide by the high-level summits.
- Threatened doctors strike is expected to paralyse hospitals.
- Attorney-general will decide by the end of this week whether to prosecute a Greek Cypriot fisherman suspected of knowingly spreading the AIDS virus to a British woman.
- Amnesty says Cyprus uses torture weapons.
- Cyprus is to lift Iraqi crude in April or May, while local chemical company Premier Chemicals clinches a $1 million pesticide supply deal.
- Allantika Grigoriou and Nikas S.A. of Greece form a joint venture.
- Vote of confidence in the future. Greek and Turkish Cypriot children in a symbolic tree-planting ceremony at the mixed village of Pyla.
- Nicosia is preparing ideas on the territorial issue which it will present at future direct talks with the Turkish side.
- Cyprus's chamber of commerce and industry calls for privatisations.
- The Cypriot government is ready for talks on the territorial issue.
- Government doctors are to go on strike on March 13.
